issue.title: PushState being ignored
issue.body:
I have a setup looking like this:

``` javascript
export const history = createBrowserHistory(); // history@1.9.0
// ...
<Router history={ history }> // react-router@1.0.0-rc1
```

When I click a `<Link to='/somepage'>` or navigate there manually (either by typing the URL or pressing back / forward) - the URL changes and the router displays the component associated with `/somepage`.

However, if I import the `history` object elsewhere, and try `history.pushState(null, '/somepage')`, or I open up the console in my browser and do `window.history.pushState(null, null, '/somepage')`, the URL changes, but nothing else happens. If I navigate back and then forward with the browser, then it works as expected.

My setup is much more elaborate than in the snippet above, but I've triple-checked the essentials, and I'm fairly certain that I'm using the correct `history` object in all places that matter. Please, help me troubleshoot this and/or confirm that this is a bug.

body: Is there any workaround to this?  I'm unable to get `history.pushState`, `history.replaceState`, nor `history.transitionTo` to actually load the component at the new url.

body:
@mjackson your fix looks good, but there might an unintended side effect.

Server rendering currently utilizes `useQueries.match`, and since that no longer mutates state, calls to `history.isActive` on the server will no longer return the correct value (hence [server rendering - renders active Links as active](https://github.com/rackt/react-router/blob/master/modules/__tests__/serverRendering-test.js#L96) failing in current build). One potential fix for this might be to transition the memory history to the correct location in `match`, as I've done here https://github.com/schnerd/react-router/commit/01bd815e893950c3be6345686ffadd648ecd525f. If that looks good, or if you have other ideas on how this might be solved, let me know and I can submit a PR.

As a quick aside, the removal of null arguments in [be37196](https://github.com/rackt/react-router/commit/be3719661b5714a15d3e70f50503450caddc3ee8#diff-58118d23f5f2a5fe2011781eb16cb7f2L55) also breaks the test [server rendering - sends null values when no routes match](https://github.com/rackt/react-router/blob/master/modules/__tests__/serverRendering-test.js#L108).
